newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's Mubarak, Arafat discuss peace "crisis".
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Mubarak, Arafat discuss peace "crisis".

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived in Egypt on Saturday and went straight into talks with President Hosni Mubarak on the crisis in the Middle East peace talks, Egyptian state television said.

The two leaders "discussed the latest developments and the crisis that the peace process is going through particularly after the dangerous decisions issued by the Israeli cabinet in the wake of the explosions that took place in west Jerusalem," the news broadcast said.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet demanded Arafat crack down on Moslem militants responsible for a double suicide bombing in a Jerusalem market on Wednesday that killed 13 people and wounded 170.

Israel also suspended peace talks with the Palestinian Authority, rounded up scores of suspected militants, closed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, demanded the extradition of the PLO police chief and threatened to re-enter Palestinian self-rule areas to seize militants if Arafat failed to do the job.

Arafat, who met Mubarak in the Egyptian leader's private residence in Burg el-Arab, near the Mediterranean city of Alexandria, was accompanied by senior Palestinian officials Saeb Erekat, Nabil Shaath and Mahmoud Abbas.
The Palestinian leader is also under fire from legislators over allegations of rampant corruption and misrule in his administration.

Sixteen out of Arafat's 18 ministers offered on Friday to resign after the Palestinian Legislative Council in a non-binding vote gave Arafat one month to dissolve his cabinet and name a new team of "qualified and experienced ministers".
Egypt has been trying to jump-start Israeli-Palestinian peace talks that collapsed after Israel began to build a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
